findings.title: Negative threshold applies the Winkler bonus instead of giving plain Jaro
findings.property: with a negative threshold, similarity equals the plain Jaro similarity (no Winkler bonus)
findings.actual: 0.7 (Winkler bonus applied, since j > threshold is always true)
findings.evidence: Constructor javadoc: 'Set threshold to a negative value to get the Jaro distance.' The code adds the bonus when j > threshold, so a negative threshold always adds it; Jaro needs threshold >= 1.

review.title: JaroWinkler(negative threshold) still applies the Winkler bonus, contradicting the constructor javadoc
review.reason: The constructor javadoc says 'Set threshold to a negative value to get the Jaro distance.' But `similarity` adds the bonus whenever `j > threshold`, and j is never negative, so a negative threshold applies the bonus on every non-zero match. For ("ab","ac") the plain Jaro value is 2/3 and the code returns about 0.7. The repro uses the API correctly, and the 1e-9 tolerance is not the issue: the result differs by 0.033, with only a small float-precision error on top. A maintainer would fix either the code (a negative threshold disables the bonus) or the javadoc.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code
